references.text: Jesus' words that the Father is in Him and He in the Father, confirmed through the works He does, are repeated directly here where Jesus explains that the words He speaks are the Father's works.
The theme of the Father working through the Son's works, and that the Son's works are proof of their unity, is central to this discussion about God's work.
The prayer that all may be one, so that the world may believe that the Father has sent the Son, builds on the same unity between Father and Son that is evidenced in John 10:38.
Jesus emphasizes that He does not speak on His own authority, but that the Father who sent Him has given Him both message and works, which is the core of the argument to believe in the works.
Jesus says that He always does what is pleasing to the Father, and that the Father is with Him, which is the same logic used when He asks people to believe in the works to know the unity.
